disclaimer: Screening assumptions only. Confirm jurisdictional determinations, local ordinances, floodplain permits, surveys, title instruments, and utility easements before design or acquisition.

profiles.label: Planning screen
profiles.description: Conservative early feasibility assumptions where parcel-specific instruments are not yet available.

profiles.label: Mapped footprints
profiles.description: Excludes mapped features only. Use for comparison, not as a regulatory conclusion.

layers.label: NWI wetlands
layers.reason: Mapped wetland footprint plus an adjustable planning review buffer.
layers.geometry_basis: Buffer outward from the mapped polygon edge.
layers.basis: The 50 ft default is an early-screening assumption, not a federal rule. Federal Section 404 regulates certain discharges; state and local programs may impose different buffers.
layers.verification: Obtain a current delineation and jurisdictional review, then apply the governing local ordinance or permit condition.

layers.label: FEMA 1% annual-chance flood hazard
layers.reason: Mapped high-risk flood hazard area; no additional lateral setback is assumed.
layers.geometry_basis: Exclude the mapped polygon; freeboard is vertical and is not represented by a planar buffer.
layers.basis: The mapped boundary is used for screening. Floodway development can require a no-rise analysis, and local ordinances may exceed NFIP minimums.
layers.verification: Confirm the effective FIRM/FIS, zone and floodway status with the local floodplain administrator and evaluate elevation requirements separately.

layers.label: Transmission corridor
layers.reason: Adjustable planning corridor measured from the mapped line centerline.
layers.geometry_basis: Buffer each side of the line centerline; the configured value is half the total assumed corridor width.
layers.basis: A 100 ft half-width represents the upper end of FERC's typical 100-200 ft total right-of-way range for relevant projects. Actual rights and restrictions come from the recorded easement and utility requirements.
layers.verification: Review title, survey the easement, identify line voltage and operator, and obtain the operator's current structure and vegetation restrictions.
